clue.text: Some seek leeway for Swiss painter

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are wanted, a run lying across the gap

blocks.note: the end of seek joined to the start of leeway

explanation.surface: A demand that a Swiss artist be given more room for manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born modernist painter, so he is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Winner here, champ ultimately surmounting great dislike

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is kept
in a down clue, a piece surmounting another sits above it, so it is written first

blocks.note: the last letter of champ
odium is intense hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: A champion stands above a rival who is widely loathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winner here' is a cryptic pointer to the place a victor stands, not a word for the victor.
explanation.definitionFit: A podium is the raised platform where a winning competitor stands to receive a medal.

clue.text: Nit-picking editor in room off kitchen

indicators.note: one item placed in another means it sits inside it, enclosed by the second

blocks.note: a pantry is a small storeroom beside a kitchen
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A fussy editor holed up in a side room, correcting every comma.
explanation.walkthrough: ED goes inside PANT|RY: PANT + ED + RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor details and rules, which is what nit-picking describes.

clue.text: Try small glass of spirits

blocks.note: first meaning: an attempt, as in have a go
second meaning: a single measure of liquor

explanation.surface: An invitation to sample a little nip of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both an attempt at something and a single small measure of strong drink.

clue.text: He protects troubled lass in difficult situation

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed and out of order, so these letters are rearranged
to protect something is to surround and shield it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters of lass rearranged

explanation.surface: A man shields an upset young woman when things get tough.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled girl's word sits between the H and E of He.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is a troublesome or annoying situation, a near synonym for a predicament.

clue.text: Banter about role, doubly English

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
an actor's part is a role
E for English, given twice

explanation.surface: Chat about acting roles, in thoroughly English style.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty conversation, the same playful exchange that banter names.

clue.text: Unexpectedly vocal, energetic to begin with, in recess

indicators.note: to begin with points at the opening letter of the word just before it
something happening unexpectedly is out of the usual order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the first letter of energetic

explanation.surface: Someone surprisingly loud and lively at first, sitting in a corner nook.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess in the wall of a room, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Cast North as ideal place

blocks.note: to heave is to throw or hurl
N is the abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: Someone sends a casting director's choice northward, seeing it as paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is used figuratively for any place of perfect happiness, so it is a perfect spot.

clue.text: Not sure what to do, hints tea should be served

indicators.note: food served is prepared and dished up, so these letters are made into something new

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An uncertain host gets a nudge that it is time to pour tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hesitant means wavering or undecided, unable to settle on a course of action.

clue.text: Personal assistant in street quarrel

indicators.note: one item being in another means it sits inside it, enclosed by the second

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
PA is the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: An office helper caught up in a row out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel or squabble, so the noun matches.

clue.text: Allow advice to person wanting hair curled?

definitions.text: advice to person wanting hair curled?
definitions.note: a phrase, read as two words

blocks.note: first meaning: to give permission

blocks.clueFragment: advice to person wanting hair curled?
blocks.note: second meaning, split in two: a hairdresser's tip to have a curling treatment done

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as two words and it becomes a hairdresser's suggestion; a perm is a chemical treatment that sets curls.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to let something happen or give consent, the plain sense of allow.

clue.text: Livingstone, say, once extremely popular, welcoming folk traditions

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, so only the first and last letters of the next word are kept
to welcome someone is to take them in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: ex means former
the first and last letters of popular
lore is a body of traditional knowledge and stories

explanation.surface: A Victorian traveller who was a hit in his day and embraced local customs.
explanation.definitionFit: David Livingstone was a famous Scottish explorer of Africa, so he is an example; 'say' flags it.

clue.text: Strange tale about river warning

indicators.note: strange means odd or abnormal, so these letters come out in an unfamiliar order
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: the letters of tale rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An odd story told around a river serves as a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal of danger, a synonym for a warning.

clue.text: Program the French put into action getting sound of welcome

blocks.note: an app is a software program
la is French for the, feminine form
to use something is to put it into action

explanation.surface: A programmer deploying French code wins a warm reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put into' looks like a container signal, but the whole phrase is the definition of a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is clapping, the noise an audience makes to greet or acclaim someone.

clue.text: Regularly pre-empt one trying to sell goods

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of pre-empt

explanation.surface: A salesman habitually gets in first before rivals can.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep, short for representative, is a travelling salesperson for a company.

clue.text: Ruthlessly ambitious person using sleight horrifies you at first

indicators.note: at first points at the opening letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A go-getter who uses trickery appals you from the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushy describes someone forcefully self-assertive in getting what they want, a near synonym.

clue.text: Dog improved with new start (second)

indicators.note: a new start means the first letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: something improved is better
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A dog trained up and given a second fresh beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: The S for second replaces the B at the front of the word for improved.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a gundog breed, such as the Irish or English setter, so it is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Expected levy not initially viable — confer

indicators.note: not with the opening letter of viable means that letter is struck out of the preceding word

blocks.note: par is the expected standard, as in golf
taken as written before a letter is removed

explanation.surface: A tax that is due is unworkable from the start, so talks are needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The V that begins viable is taken out of levy.
explanation.definitionFit: To parley is to hold talks, especially with an opponent, a synonym for confer.

clue.text: Music performer's protective cover, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals a word that is only sounded like the clue's meaning, not spelt the same

blocks.note: a wrapper is a covering for something; the W is silent

explanation.surface: A singer's coat or casing, as people say.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapper is a performer of rap music, so the answer is a kind of musical artist.

clue.text: Milton, say, old favourite around

indicators.note: around means one piece encircles the other, placing it inside

blocks.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A much-loved writer from the past, still widely read.
explanation.definitionFit: John Milton wrote Paradise Lost, so he is an example of a poet, as 'say' signals.

clue.text: Feature of football got pal so excited

indicators.note: being excited means agitated and stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A friend's thrilling football match got him worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A goalpost is one of the two uprights that form a football goal, a fixture of every pitch.

clue.text: Game after Foxtrot?

definitions.note: describes what follows Foxtrot rather than naming a word

blocks.note: first meaning: a sport played with clubs and a ball
second meaning: the code word for G, which follows F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot looks like a dance, but it is the radio code word for F, and the next letter's code word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sport played over a course, and also stands for G in the radio spelling alphabet.

clue.text: Moved fast, exercising in South Dakota

indicators.note: one item being in another means it sits inside it, enclosed by the second

blocks.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
PE is physical education, i.e. exercise

explanation.surface: Someone raced along while working out on the plains.
explanation.definitionFit: Sped is the past tense of speed, so it means travelled quickly.

clue.text: Ring again for annulment?

blocks.note: first meaning: sound the bells once more
second meaning: the cancelling of a law

explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE (again) plus PEAL (ring of bells), the word means to ring once more; the question mark flags this whimsical split.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeal is the formal revoking of a law, the same idea as an annulment.

clue.text: Kitchen item, jug, at back of empty sink

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters
being at the back of something means it comes after it in the answer

blocks.note: the first and last letters of sink
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A jug is left at the back of a drained kitchen sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A skewer is a metal or wooden spike for holding food while cooking, so it is a kitchen utensil.
